body:
## Context

PR16's `groupIssues` returns `fanout: {mode, concurrencyCap}` (work-driver.ts:1193-1204, default `MAX_PARALLEL_GROUPS_DEFAULT=2` at :991, env `PI_ENSEMBLE_PARALLEL_GROUPS`) but commands.ts:262 destructures only `{groups, notes}` and runs groups strictly sequentially (for-loop :275-320, halt-on-non-merged :305-319). Target: K groups run concurrently; the ONLY serialized section is integration at repoRoot (apply + commit + push + `gh pr create` — a few seconds), guarded by an in-process async mutex. One Pi process owns all groups, so a promise-chain mutex is sufficient and total; no lockfile.

Sequencing note: requires PR-A ("repoRoot is never a dev tree") and PR-D (concurrency guards) merged first — turning concurrency on without them re-creates #602 and the unthrottled fanout. This work must ship as its own separate PR, independent of any other open issue.

## What to build

**A. Bounded pool** (commands.ts:262,275-320): destructure `{groups, notes, fanout}`; replace the for-loop with a shared-index pool of `fanout.concurrencyCap` workers. New knob `PI_ENSEMBLE_PARALLEL_WORK=0` forces the old sequential loop. `setupWorkspaceTmp` (work-driver.ts:287-303) runs once before fan-out (module-level `once` guard — it writes the shared `.git/info/exclude`).

**B. Halt semantics:** shared `halted` flag. Worker checks the flag before claiming the next group. On a group ending `status !== "merged"` or throwing → set flag, emit today's halt message listing NOT-started groups; in-flight groups run to completion; failed group hands off exactly as today. Final summary: merged / handed-off / not-started.

**C. Integration mutex** (work-driver.ts): `let integrationChain: Promise<void>` + `export async function withIntegrationLock<T>(fn)` (chain-and-await, release in try/finally). `runCommitPr` wraps the contiguous span: preflight-clean → `checkout -B` → apply patches → commit → push → `gh pr create` → `verifyConsolidation` (:2141) → `verifyStepOutcome` rev-list (:2534) — release only after both gates (they read repoRoot HEAD). The lens-fix re-integrate uses the same lock. Integration failure releases the lock and routes that group to handoff; it does not by itself halt the queue (the group's terminal status does, via B).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Offline two-group test through `runWorkDriver` (injected `dispatchFn`/`verifyExecFn`): commit-pr spans sleep inside the lock recording enter/exit timestamps → asserted non-overlapping.
- [ ] 3-group fixture, group 1 fails mid-flight → group 2 (in-flight) finishes, group 3 never starts, halt message lists it.
- [ ] cap=1 fixture reproduces today's sequential event log byte-for-byte.
- [ ] `PI_ENSEMBLE_PARALLEL_WORK=0` restores the sequential for-loop.
- [ ] `setupWorkspaceTmp` runs exactly once under fan-out.
- [ ] Lock released on integration throw (try/finally test).
- [ ] tsc + biome + smokes green; docs updated (parallel-mode section + env knobs).

## Out of scope

Raising the group cap above 2; spawn caps/widget (PR-D); worktree mechanics (PR-A); grouping rules R1-R5 and `groupIssues` output shape; cross-invocation parallelism (pool lives inside one `/work` invocation).

## Test plan

Offline: fixtures above. Live on lantern: `/work` with two independent small issues; verify two PRs, non-interleaved integration commits, correct halt behavior by forcing one group's CI to fail.

---
title: feat(work): parallel group queue with bounded pool + repoRoot integration mutex
